project_metadata.job_description: Seeking a skilled CAD design engineer to convert measured parts from photos into STEP or Inventor 3D files, including manufacturing drawings. The ideal candidate will have experience in precision engineering and be able to accurately translate 2D measurements into 3D models. Attention to detail and the ability to deliver high-quality designs are essential.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Yes, of course. This is actually how most of my projects are done—working from photos with dimensions marked on them.
I'm definitely open to long-term cooperation.
Best regards,
Alexander

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Thank you for the offer.
If it works for you, I would prefer to complete this first project on a fixed-price basis.
Based on the project description, I can offer $500 fixed with an estimated delivery time of 4–6 days.
What do you think?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Could you also please confirm:
Which steel grade should be used for the shaft and the other parts?
Whether you have a company drawing template or specific ČSN/EN ISO requirements.
During the work, some dimensions may need additional clarification, so please stay available for questions and quick confirmation.

messages.text:

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
No worries at all, Lukas.
Everyone starts somewhere. I'll help make the process as smooth as possible, and if there are any questions about the platform, just let me know.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hi, please take a look at this part. How should it be manufactured: as one solid piece, or as a separate ring with four welded lugs? From the photo, I can see that it is welded to the flange, but I cannot determine whether the lugs are welded to the ring or if the ring and lugs are made as one piece.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
At this stage, I have created the assembly. Some dimensions are missing, and several dimensions do not match. It is also not completely clear where the two separate parts should be installed.
I have prepared a list of clarification questions and am waiting for your answers. After receiving them, I will adjust the model and send you a sectional view of the assembly based on the dimensions currently available. Further corrections may still be required afterward.
I look forward to your feedback.

Hi Lukas,
Okay, understood. Tomorrow I'll review everything, make the necessary revisions, and prepare a preliminary drawing for your review.
Best regards,
Alexander

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Could you please let me know the model of the sheet unwinder?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
There are still a few unclear points regarding the bushing. As I understand it, the three holes are intended for fastening it with screws. However, at the same time, there appears to be a very large interference fit: the outer diameter of the bushing is 61.2 mm, while the bore in the mating part is 60 mm
The countersinks also look as though they are intended to recess the heads of countersunk screws, but in that case the bushing appears to be installed from the opposite side. Could you please clarify how this assembly is actually put together?
It is also clear that some components of the complete shaft assembly are missing from the photos. Because of this, the operating principle of the mechanism is not yet fully clear.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I have added the dimensions we have obtained so far. Please note that this is not the final drawing — it is only a preview for confirming the final dimensions. Please remeasure the indicated dimensions or simply confirm them.
The shaft is shown assembled in its fully retracted position.

messages.text: Hi, do you have Telegram for quicker communication?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Good evening, Lukas.
Please find attached the first fully prepared version of the drawings. Since I have not yet received information about how the bushing should be installed and secured, please ignore its current design. At the moment, it is shown simply secured with three screws.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Good afternoon, Lukas. Is everything clear so far? Do you have any comments, corrections, or additional requests? When should I expect your feedback?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Hi, currently working on it, I\`ll come back to you today with all clarification, hopefully. Thanks for your patience .

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello Alex,
finally I've been able to check everything and review your drawings.

1\. Main difference, which I wasn't aware about is that we need to produce premachined parts, weld them together and then do the final machining. We are talking about POS 1+2+3.

2\. Main shaft raw input material is tube 108/28 and will be premachined in order to secure positions for POS 2+3.

3\. The bushing which was not clear is located inside the main shaft (**IMPORTANT**: in my notes, there is this information incorrect - the bushing is not mounted to the POS 4 but in main shaft only) - please choose suitable clearance to fit bushing and shaft.

4\. On POS 4 is mounted piston/rod end with nut. This rod from control piston (securing the sliding movement) is inside the main shaft (that's why the inner dia of 55mm must be also machined after welding).

5\. The cross section C-C on mainshaft drw. indicates this keyway will not be there, the request is to make the thread for locking nut M100x2 wider; also space for main bushing is requested wider (40mm)

6\. If possible, please use numbering of drawings as shown on assembly

Let me know the progress and thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Now the bushing arrangement looks logical. However, one more point: are you sure about its length? The bushing seems rather short compared with the machined seat inside the shaft.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Should these lugs be aligned in the same plane, correct? In the photos, they appear to be offset, so I assumed that was intentional.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: No, no, as written in message (incorrect written on the drawings), the bushing is placed inside the main shaft and thru this bushing in guided rod from control piston - so you need to choose suitable clearance (i.e H8/h9) for bushing and inner diameter of shaft. On the sliding part there is only the end of the piston

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: 45 degrees between the holes axis, so as shown on picture and as you have it on the assembly

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I think I’m getting confused again. Does this mean that the bushing no longer needs to be secured with screws if it is installed only inside the main shaft?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: And with a clearance fit, won’t the bushing simply be loose and move around inside the shaft?Or is the bushing rigidly fitted onto the piston rod?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Face 1 is flat, so I do not think we need to leave a machining allowance on it. After welding, it would not be possible to machine this face on a lathe while keeping it flat. However, I think we can add a machining allowance on face 2. Alternatively, we could leave a machining allowance on face 1 as well and machine it flat on a milling machine after welding. What do you think?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I was told that this bushing is really only in the shaft. Or I\`m thinking about other possible solution, that the bushing is also secured in the sliding end with the rod nut thru and the bushing is really sliding inside the main shaft and the contact surface is outside diameter of the bushing. Please prepare it like that, after you finalize the drawings I will present it to the maintanence manager and perhaps he will come with other idea. At the moment, do it please like this.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: So, should we remove the holes in the bushing now, or leave them both in the bushing and in the sliding mandrel?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
You\`re right, surface 1 without machining after welding.
Surface 2 also. Because it will be very bad for machining. So these surfaces must be finalized before welded on shaft. Is that ok?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Please keep them as it is.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: ок

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Perfect, thank you

messages.speaker: client

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hi, do you have any other projects at the moment? I have some available time and can work on them in parallel :)

messages.text:
Hi, sorry for my late reply. I\`m travelling for few days on business trip. I will review your drawings probably today at night.
If everything is fine without any further comments than I will release the payment.
Is it OK for you like that?
And if there will be any notes from production manager, are you willing to update drawings even after we “close” this project?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hi Lukas, yes, that’s fine. I’ll wait for your feedback. If anything needs to be corrected, just write to me — I’m almost always available. We’ll finalize and fix everything needed.

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Good evening,
I\`ve checked the drawings, to be honest, the version without colours is better to read, maybe the 3D views could be coloured, but all other views without.
There are really minor things to be corrected, please see notes in the drawings.

After we finalize this project, if possible, could you provide not only pdf files but dwg/dxf files as well ?
And the 3D files will be only step files from you? Any chance to get “live format” like .ipt and .idw??

Thank you for updating.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi Lukas, yes, of course. I can export the drawings to DWG/DXF — no problem.
I will also provide the 3D models in STEP format and the original editable SolidWorks files: SLDPRT, SLDASM and SLDDRW. In addition to STEP, I can export the models to SAT, IGES or IFC formats.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: If this dimension is added, it will duplicate the overall dimension, which is already shown as a minimum and maximum value corresponding to the full travel. So, should I leave the current overall dimension, or remove it and add the dimension you indicated instead?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Overall length is fine, but functional dimension is the one between those holes. So this add and the overall maybe in bracket.
Please provide final set of drawings in pdf, I will confirm them and then you can make the export to other formats.
Regarding the formats: PDF+DWG and STEP+ editable solidworks 3D files and drawings.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: ok

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hi,
Thank you for the final revision. To be honest the drawings look quite good. As I wrote, if there\`ll be any further small changes, are you willing to implement them even if we close this project?
And you can release all files as agreed earlier.
Thank you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Yes, of course. I am almost always available. I also look forward to working with you on future projects.
Should any small adjustments be needed, just message me and I will make them promptly.

messages.text: I’ve released the payment, hopefully you get it soon.
